blogs.title: DeepSeekMath, Explained: How a 7B Open Model Learns to Do Competition-Level Math
blogs.description: A plain-English tour of the project: why math is hard for language models, how DeepSeekMath 7B hits 51.7% on the MATH benchmark without tools or voting (and 60.9% with 64-sample self-consistency), and what this means for open AI as it nears GPT-4/Gemini-Ultra on math. Covers the training recipe (code-initialized base, 500B tokens, 120B math tokens), bilingual gains, and highlights across step-by-step reasoning, code-aided problem solving, and formal proofs.

blogs.title: Mining Math from the Open Web: Inside the 120B-Token DeepSeekMath Corpus
blogs.description: How the team turned Common Crawl into a high-quality, multilingual math dataset at scale. Walks through the iterative fastText-based classifier, domain-level mining, human-in-the-loop refinement, deduplication, and benchmark decontamination (10-gram filtering). Explains why this corpus outperforms MathPile, OpenWebMath, and Proof-Pile-2 in learning curves and downstream results—and shares practical takeaways for building domain-specific corpora.

blogs.title: Does Coding Improve Reasoning? What DeepSeekMath Teaches Us
blogs.description: A deep dive into the training ablations showing that code pretraining boosts mathematical reasoning—with and without tools. Unpacks two-stage (code → math) versus one-stage (code+math mix) setups, trade-offs like catastrophic forgetting, and why mixed training can preserve coding while strengthening program-aided math. Also covers surprising spillover gains on MMLU and BBH, suggesting broader reasoning benefits.

blogs.title: From CoT to Code: How Instruction Tuning and Tool Use Power DeepSeekMath
blogs.description: Explains the 776K-example instruction-tuning set spanning chain-of-thought, program-of-thought, and tool-integrated reasoning in English and Chinese. Shows how DeepSeekMath-Instruct 7B beats other 7B models and rivals some 70B models, and why allowing Python (e.g., sympy) pushes accuracy close to 60% on MATH. Clarifies when natural-language reasoning suffices and when code execution unlocks harder problems.

blogs.title: GRPO in Plain Terms: A Leaner, Meaner Alternative to PPO for Math Reasoning
blogs.description: Demystifies Group Relative Policy Optimization, a critic-free spin on PPO that uses group-based baselines instead of a value model, reducing memory cost. Covers outcome vs process supervision, KL regularization differences, and iterative RL with reward-model refresh. Shares the key wins: boosting GSM8K from 82.9% to 88.2% and MATH from 46.8% to 51.7% using only a subset of instruction-tuning data—plus improvements on out-of-domain tasks.

blogs.title: A Field Guide to Alignment Methods—SFT, RFT, DPO, PPO, GRPO—Through One Unifying Lens
blogs.description: Translates the paper’s unified paradigm into approachable terms: how data source (online vs offline), reward function, and algorithm shape the gradient signal. Compares methods side-by-side and explains a key finding—RL improves Maj@K more than Pass@K—meaning it stabilizes the distribution toward correct answers rather than inventing new skills outright. Outlines where alignment goes next: better reward generalization, weak-to-strong training, and smarter sampling.

blogs.title: Surprises, Limits, and What’s Next: ArXiv Isn’t Magic, Geometry Is Hard
blogs.description: Highlights counterintuitive results (arXiv-heavy corpora didn’t help much on math reasoning), current weaknesses (geometry, some theorem-proof tasks), and few-shot gaps versus GPT-4. Sketches the roadmap: richer data coverage, advanced decoding (e.g., tree search), more robust RL under noisy rewards, and stronger, uncertainty-aware reward models. A candid look at where open math LLMs go from here.
